items.sentence: The dogs ___ barking at the tricycle outside our gate.
items.why: The subject 'dogs' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.

items.sentence: My brother ___ basketball every Saturday at the covered court.
items.why: 'My brother' is one person, so the verb needs an -s: 'plays'.

items.sentence: Lyka ___ to school by jeepney every morning.
items.why: 'Lyka' is singular, so the verb takes -es: 'goes'.

items.sentence: The students ___ lining up for the flag ceremony.
items.why: 'Students' is plural, so use 'are'.

items.sentence: Tita Nena ___ halo-halo at her sari-sari store.
items.why: 'Tita Nena' is one person, so the verb ends in -s: 'sells'.

items.sentence: My cousins ___ online games every night after dinner.
items.why: 'Cousins' is plural, so the verb has no -s: 'play'.

items.sentence: The jeepney ___ always full at seven in the morning.
items.why: 'The jeepney' is one thing, so use 'is'.

items.sentence: Marco and Jom ___ members of the school basketball team.
items.why: 'Marco and Jom' means two people, so use 'are'.

items.sentence: The rain ___ falling hard, so classes are suspended today.
items.why: 'The rain' is singular, so use 'is'.

items.sentence: My mother ___ in Dubai as a caregiver.
items.why: 'My mother' is one person, so the verb ends in -s: 'works'.

items.sentence: Bea forgot her load, so ___ borrowed my phone.
items.why: Bea is a girl doing the action, so the subject pronoun is 'she'.

items.sentence: Jom and I are late, so please wait for ___.
items.why: After 'wait for', use the object pronoun 'us' for 'Jom and I'.

items.sentence: My father works abroad, and I miss ___ so much.
items.why: 'Father' receives the action 'miss', so use the object pronoun 'him'.

items.sentence: The players are tired because ___ practiced all afternoon.
items.why: 'Players' is plural and does the action, so use 'they'.

items.sentence: Lyka baked bibingka, and ___ gave some to the teachers.
items.why: Lyka is the one giving, so use the subject pronoun 'she'.

items.sentence: The tricycle is old, but ___ still runs well.
items.why: A tricycle is a thing, so use 'it'.

items.sentence: Tita Nena called the kids and told ___ to come home.
items.why: 'The kids' receive the telling, so use the object pronoun 'them'.

items.sentence: Marco is my best friend, and I always sit beside ___.
items.why: After 'beside', use the object pronoun 'him' for Marco.

items.sentence: The teacher gave ___ a new notebook for the project.
items.why: The notebook was given to the speaker, so use the object pronoun 'me'.

items.sentence: Kuya Ron and Bea are coming, and ___ will bring the ball.
items.why: 'Kuya Ron and Bea' are two people doing the action, so use 'they'.

items.sentence: It took ___ hour to reach the mall by jeepney.
items.why: 'Hour' starts with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so use 'an'.

items.sentence: Bea is ___ university student now, but she still rides the jeepney.
items.why: 'University' starts with a 'yu' sound, not a vowel sound, so use 'a'.

items.sentence: Lyka brought ___ umbrella because of the heavy rain.
items.why: 'Umbrella' starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an'.

items.sentence: Jom is ___ only boy in his family.
items.why: 'Only' points to one specific person, so use 'the'.

items.sentence: Marco wants to be ___ honest barangay captain someday.
items.why: 'Honest' starts with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so use 'an'.

items.sentence: Tita Nena bought ___ new rice cooker at the market.
items.why: 'New' starts with a consonant sound, so use 'a' for one rice cooker.

items.sentence: ___ sun is very hot at noon during fiesta season.
items.why: There is only one sun, so use 'the'.

items.sentence: Kuya Ron is ___ oldest of five children.
items.why: Words like 'oldest' point to one specific person, so use 'the'.

items.sentence: Lyka ate ___ egg and rice before the flag ceremony.
items.why: 'Egg' starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an'.

items.sentence: There is ___ basketball tournament at the plaza tonight.
items.why: 'Basketball' starts with a consonant sound, so use 'a'.

items.sentence: Many ___ ride the jeepney to school every day.
items.why: The plural of 'child' is the irregular word 'children'.

items.sentence: Marco hurt both of his ___ during the basketball game.
items.why: The plural of 'foot' is the irregular word 'feet'.

items.sentence: Lyka brushes her ___ before she goes to bed.
items.why: The plural of 'tooth' is the irregular word 'teeth'.

items.sentence: Many ___ crowded the plaza for the fiesta.
items.why: 'People' is already plural; it means more than one person.

items.sentence: Two ___ ran across the sari-sari store floor last night.
items.why: The plural of 'mouse' is the irregular word 'mice'.

items.sentence: Bea packed two ___ of rice for merienda.
items.why: Words ending in -x add -es to make the plural: 'boxes'.

items.sentence: The ___ at the terminal are waiting for passengers.
items.why: Most words just add -s to make the plural: 'tricycles'.

items.sentence: The new ___ on the court are made of steel.
items.why: Words ending in -ch add -es to make the plural: 'benches'.

items.sentence: Jom watched three ___ on TikTok before class.
items.why: 'Video' just adds -s to make the plural: 'videos'.

items.sentence: Several ___ hit the province last year.
items.why: Most words just add -s to make the plural: 'typhoons'.
